source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MCPE-188694:The Elytra animation only plays in 3rd person, not 1st person
source_meta._title: Elytra appearance doesn't update in 1st person mode; only in 3rd person

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.9.2 using a vanilla singleplayer Creative-mode Superflat world and keyboard/mouse controls. Use the perspective-toggle control, which is F5 by default, and the jump control, which is Space by default. The report also confirms that the issue can occur in multiplayer, but multiplayer is not required for this reproduction path.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition 1.9.2 game version; do not substitute the listed fix version 24w33a.
Use an unmodified client so that mods do not replace the player or Elytra renderer.
Know the current key bindings for Jump and Toggle Perspective. The instructions use their defaults: Space and F5.
The test needs enough height and airtime to begin gliding while in first-person view. The procedure therefore creates an elevated standing block over a clear landing area.
An Elytra must be equipped in the player's chest armor slot before the perspective and gliding sequence begins.

steps.action: From the Minecraft Launcher, start the installation corresponding to Java Edition 1.9.2. At the main menu, select Singleplayer and then Create New World.
steps.exact_input: Launcher version: 1.9.2; Main menu -> Singleplayer -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open in Minecraft Java Edition 1.9.2.

steps.action: Configure a simple world for safe and deterministic setup. Change Game Mode to Creative. Open More World Options, cycle World Type until Superflat is selected, return with Done, and create the world. No particular seed is required by the report.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; More World Options... -> World Type: Superflat -> Done -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: A Creative-mode Superflat world begins loading.

steps.action: Wait before interacting. Continue only after the flat terrain has rendered around the player and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby chunks are visible, the player is standing on the flat surface, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory control, which is E by default. Select the Search Items tab; if necessary, identify it by hovering over the Creative inventory tabs until the Search Items tooltip appears.
steps.exact_input: E; select Search Items
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open with a text search field available.

steps.action: Click the search field, enter "elytra", and move one Elytra from the search results into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the inventory.
steps.exact_input: elytra
steps.success_cue: An Elytra is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Open the Survival Inventory tab within the Creative inventory. Drag the Elytra from its hotbar slot into the chest armor slot beside the player model. The chest slot is the second armor slot from the top, between the helmet and leggings slots.
steps.exact_input: Drag Elytra from hotbar to chest armor slot
steps.success_cue: The Elytra is displayed in the chest armor slot on the inventory screen.

steps.action: Return to the Search Items tab, replace the search text with "stone", and place a stack of Stone into another empty hotbar slot. Any solid full block would satisfy the report, but Stone provides a simple elevated standing block.
steps.exact_input: stone
steps.success_cue: The Elytra remains equipped and a stack of Stone is available in the hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E. Select the Stone hotbar slot by pressing its corresponding number key from 1 through 9 or by using the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E; then the number key corresponding to the Stone hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible and Stone appears as the selected item in the player's hand.

steps.action: Build a vertical pillar approximately 25 blocks tall over the flat, unobstructed ground. Place the first Stone on the ground, stand on it, then repeatedly perform a single jump and right-click the top face beneath the player to place the next block. Allow each jump to finish before starting the next so that Creative flight is not accidentally activated. Count at least 25 placed blocks.
steps.exact_input: Right-click to place; then repeat Space followed by right-click at least 24 more times
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the top block of an approximately 25-block-high Stone pillar, with clear air around the pillar and flat ground below.

steps.action: Stop all movement and stand near the center of the pillar's top block. Verify that the player is standing on the block rather than hovering in Creative flight. If flight was accidentally activated, double-tap Space to disable it and settle onto the top block before continuing.
steps.exact_input: Release movement controls; if hovering, double-tap Space once and land on the top block
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on the top Stone block and will fall if they move beyond its edge.

steps.action: Establish first-person view before performing the report's required perspective cycle. Press the Toggle Perspective key as many times as necessary until the player's body is no longer shown in front of the camera and only the normal first-person hand or held item is visible.
steps.exact_input: F5 as needed until first-person view is active
steps.success_cue: The camera is in first-person view.

steps.action: While still standing on the top block, press the Toggle Perspective key once to enter rear third-person view.
steps.exact_input: F5
steps.success_cue: The camera is behind the player, and the player's back and equipped Elytra are visible while the player remains standing on the pillar.

steps.action: Return to first-person view before gliding. In Java Edition 1.9.2, the perspective control cycles through rear third-person, front third-person, and first-person, so press F5 twice, pausing briefly after each press.
steps.exact_input: F5, brief pause, F5
steps.success_cue: The player is again in first-person view and is still standing on the top block.

steps.action: Aim the camera outward over the clear landing area, approximately toward the horizon or slightly downward. Do not change perspective again yet.
steps.exact_input: Move mouse to aim outward, approximately level or slightly downward
steps.success_cue: The first-person camera points away from the pillar into unobstructed air, with room to glide before reaching the ground.

steps.action: Walk forward off the top block using the forward control, W by default. Release W after the player has cleared the edge, and remain in first-person view.
steps.exact_input: W until clear of the block, then release W
steps.success_cue: The player is airborne, falling away from the pillar, and is still in first-person view.

steps.action: Once the player has begun descending, press the Jump control once to start gliding with the equipped Elytra. In this affected historical version, the input must be made while falling rather than while still rising.
steps.exact_input: Space once while falling
steps.success_cue: The trajectory changes from a mostly vertical fall to forward Elytra gliding, with a slower descent and continued clearance above the ground.

steps.action: Allow only enough time to confirm that gliding is active. Keep the camera aimed forward and do not wait until the player is close to landing.
steps.success_cue: The player is actively moving forward through the air in first-person Elytra glide and still has several blocks of altitude remaining.

steps.action: While the player is still actively gliding, press the Toggle Perspective key exactly once to change directly from first-person view to rear third-person view. This perspective change is the trigger; do not press F5 again and do not wait for landing before handing off.
steps.exact_input: F5 once while actively gliding
steps.success_cue: The camera has just entered rear third-person view, the airborne player and equipped Elytra are visible, and the player remains in the glide before landing.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just changed from first-person to rear third-person view while actively gliding with an equipped Elytra and remains airborne. Begin observation immediately, before another perspective change or landing occurs.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, world type, or required platform height. Creative mode, a Superflat world, and an approximately 25-block pillar are practical setup choices that provide the necessary airtime without adding exploration or survival hazards.

The report's instruction to "Stand on a block" does not explicitly state that the block must be elevated. Elevation is inferred because the following instruction requires starting an Elytra glide while remaining airborne long enough to switch perspective.
Singleplayer is selected as the minimum deterministic environment. A report comment confirms that multiplayer is also affected, but does not state that multiplayer is required.
The report does not state whether controls are rebound. F5, Space, E, and W refer to the default Java Edition keyboard bindings; use the corresponding bound actions if the local controls differ.

Only the primary sequence—begin gliding in first-person and then enter third-person—is included. The report also describes a reverse landing variant, but repeating that variant is not necessary to reach the primary trigger state.

source_meta._title: Hand animation still plays when 7 blocks under a boat

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 20w28a in a single-player Creative-mode world with commands enabled. Use first-person view with the HUD and player hand visible. The seed and world type are unrestricted, but the player must have an unobstructed standing position with sufficient empty space overhead for a boat summoned 6.5 blocks above the player's feet.
preconditions: Minecraft Java Edition 20w28a is installed and selected in the launcher.
A single-player world can be created or opened in Creative mode with commands enabled.
The player can use the Use Item/Place Block control, which is the right mouse button by default.
The test location has solid ground and at least 8 blocks of unobstructed vertical space above the player.
The player is not flying and can remain standing at the exact position from which the boat is summoned.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition using the 20w28a installation.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is displayed and identifies the running version as 20w28a.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode, or open an existing command-enabled Creative-mode world. For a new world, navigate through Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and create the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded world in Creative mode and can execute commands.

steps.action: Wait for the nearby terrain to finish rendering, then walk to a place where the player can stand on solid ground with at least 8 blocks of empty space directly overhead. Stop walking and do not enter Creative flight.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on the ground, movement responds normally, and no blocks occupy the space where the overhead boat will appear.

steps.action: Use first-person view and ensure the HUD is visible. If necessary, press F5 until first-person view is active. If the HUD, crosshair, or hand is hidden, press F1 once to show them.
steps.exact_input: F5 as needed; F1 only if the HUD is hidden
steps.success_cue: The center crosshair and hotbar are visible, and the player's hand or arm is rendered at the edge of the screen.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so the main hand contains no item. Press the number key corresponding to an empty slot; if necessary, open the inventory with E and clear one hotbar slot first.
steps.exact_input: 1-9 for an empty hotbar slot; E only if a slot must be cleared
steps.success_cue: The highlighted hotbar slot is empty and the player's empty hand is visible in first-person view.

steps.action: Without changing the player's standing position, open the in-game chat.
steps.exact_input: T
steps.success_cue: The chat command-entry field is open and ready for input.

steps.action: Enter the report's summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /summon minecraft:boat ~ ~6.5 ~ {NoGravity:1b}
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and a boat is summoned directly above the player's command-execution position.

steps.action: Do not walk, jump, or fly after summoning the boat. Rotate the camera upward until the summoned boat is visible, and allow any brief entity rendering delay to finish.
steps.success_cue: The boat is visible directly overhead, remains suspended instead of falling, and the player is still standing at the summon position.

steps.action: Adjust only the camera angle until the center crosshair is placed on the underside or side of the suspended boat. Do not move closer to it.
steps.exact_input: Move mouse to aim; do not use movement keys
steps.success_cue: The crosshair visually overlaps the boat while the player remains at the original position beneath it.

steps.action: Press the Use Item/Place Block control exactly once to attempt to ride the distant boat. Do not hold the button or repeat the interaction before handing off to observation.
steps.exact_input: Right mouse button once
steps.success_cue: One interaction input has just been sent while the crosshair is on the suspended boat and the player remains beneath it.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just right-clicked the suspended boat once from the unchanged position beneath it. Begin observation immediately after that single interaction input, without moving, clicking again, or evaluating the result during setup.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a seed, world type, or coordinates, so any unobstructed test location is used.
The report does not specify single-player versus multiplayer; single-player is selected as the simplest deterministic environment because no dedicated-server or additional-player condition is stated.
First-person view, a visible HUD, and an empty main hand are practical choices to make the relevant hand movement easy to observe; the report does not explicitly state that these are mandatory.
The supplied command is preserved exactly for 20w28a and was not replaced with syntax from another version.

source_meta._title: The main hand is positioned incorrectly when holding a loaded crossbow in your offhand

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.17 Pre-release 4 in a local single-player world. Use Creative mode as a deterministic way to obtain the crossbow and arrow. Perform the reproduction in first-person view. No specific world seed, coordinates, server, graphics setting, or multiplayer configuration is required by the report.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected version 1.17 Pre-release 4 rather than the listed fix version.
Use a newly created or existing world in which the player can obtain a crossbow and at least one arrow; the plan uses a new Creative-mode world for convenience.
Begin with the offhand slot empty.
Use the configured equivalents if the default controls E (Inventory), F (Swap Item With Offhand), F5 (Change Perspective), or right mouse button (Use Item/Place Block) have been rebound.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation that uses exactly Java Edition version 1.17 Pre-release 4, and launch it.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft Launcher -> Installations -> select/create an installation for "1.17 Pre-release 4" -> Play
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen has loaded and identifies the running version as 1.17 Pre-release 4.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a world in Creative mode. No particular seed or world-generation setting is needed. Enter the world and wait until nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded world in Creative mode, with normal movement and camera response.

steps.action: Set the camera to first-person view. Press the Change Perspective control repeatedly if necessary; its default key is F5.
steps.exact_input: F5, repeated only until first-person view is active
steps.success_cue: The camera looks directly from the player's viewpoint rather than showing the player's full character model in front of or behind the camera.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the Inventory control, whose default key is E.
steps.exact_input: E
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open.

steps.action: Use the Creative inventory's Search Items tab to find a Crossbow. Place one Crossbow into an otherwise empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the nine-slot row shown at the bottom of the screen. Remember which numbered slot, from 1 through 9, received the Crossbow.
steps.exact_input: Search Items -> enter "crossbow" -> move one Crossbow to an empty hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: One Crossbow is present in a known hotbar slot.

steps.action: Search for an Arrow and place at least one Arrow in the inventory or in a different hotbar slot. Do not replace the Crossbow, and do not put the Arrow in the hotbar slot containing the Crossbow.
steps.exact_input: Search Items -> replace the search text with "arrow" -> move at least one Arrow to a different slot
steps.success_cue: The inventory contains a Crossbow and at least one Arrow in separate slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory, then select the hotbar slot containing the Crossbow by pressing its number key or scrolling to it. Confirm that the offhand is still empty before continuing.
steps.exact_input: E, then the number key 1-9 corresponding to the Crossbow's hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The Crossbow is selected and visible in the main hand, at least one Arrow remains elsewhere in the inventory, and the offhand is empty.

steps.action: Move the Crossbow from the main hand to the offhand using the Swap Item With Offhand control, whose default key is F. Because the offhand was empty, the selected main-hand hotbar slot becomes empty.
steps.exact_input: F
steps.success_cue: The Crossbow is visible on the offhand side of the first-person view, while the currently selected main-hand hotbar slot is empty.

steps.action: Begin charging the offhand Crossbow by pressing and holding the Use Item/Place Block control, whose default input is the right mouse button. Keep holding it; do not release during the initial drawing animation.
steps.exact_input: Press and hold Right Mouse Button
steps.success_cue: The offhand Crossbow is undergoing its drawing/loading animation, and the right mouse button remains held.

steps.action: Continue holding the right mouse button until the Crossbow finishes drawing and its loading sound sequence completes. Then release the right mouse button so that the Crossbow remains charged in the offhand. Do not swap hands, select another hotbar slot, fire the Crossbow, or leave first-person view after releasing the button.
steps.exact_input: Release Right Mouse Button only after the Crossbow has fully charged
steps.success_cue: A loaded Crossbow remains equipped in the offhand, the selected main-hand slot remains empty, and the camera remains in first-person view.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just released the Use Item control after fully charging the Crossbow. The loaded Crossbow is equipped in the offhand, the selected main-hand hotbar slot is empty, and first-person view remains active. Hand control to the observation subsystem without firing the Crossbow or changing either hand's equipment.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world type, seed, or acquisition method. A new Creative-mode single-player world is used only as the simplest deterministic way to obtain the required items.

The report says to watch how the main hand is displayed but does not explicitly name the camera perspective. First-person view is selected because it directly exposes the rendered hand model being inspected.

The report does not require a dedicated server, additional players, particular coordinates, a particular main-hand preference, or special graphics settings; none are added to the reproduction requirements.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-199467:Certain entity animations stop after they've existed in world for too long
source_meta._title: View Bobbing stops working after long elytra flight

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.18.1 in a newly created single-player Creative-mode world. Use a first-person camera with the hand and hotbar visible, keep View Bobbing enabled, equip an Elytra in the chest equipment slot, and carry Firework Rockets in the hotbar. Perform the flight and final walking test in the same uninterrupted world session.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected Java Edition version 1.18.1; do not use the listed fix version 25w45a.
Allow approximately two hours of uninterrupted active play for sustained Elytra travel and generation of new chunks.
Use a newly created world so that extended straight-line travel consistently enters terrain that has not previously been generated.

Keep the world loaded for the entire reproduction. Do not use Save and Quit to Title, close the world, restart the game, or otherwise reload the world between the long flight and the final walking action; the report comment states that reloading the world removes the condition.
Default controls are assumed. If controls are rebound, use the bindings for Jump/Fly, Move Forward, Use Item, Change Perspective, and Toggle HUD that correspond to the stated default inputs.

steps.action: Launch the Minecraft Launcher, select the Java Edition installation for version 1.18.1, and start the game.
steps.exact_input: Select the 1.18.1 installation and click Play.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition 1.18.1 title screen is displayed.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode. From the title screen, open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, change Game Mode until it reads Creative, and create the world. No particular seed is specified by the report.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is present in a newly generated Creative-mode world.

steps.action: Wait for initial world loading to finish before changing settings or beginning travel.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Ensure the camera is in first-person view and that the hand and hotbar are visible. Press the perspective key repeatedly only if necessary, and restore the HUD if it is hidden.
steps.exact_input: Default: F5 cycles perspectives; F1 toggles the HUD and hand visibility.
steps.success_cue: The view is from the player's eyes, and the hotbar plus the player's hand or held item can be seen.

steps.action: Open the video settings menu that contains the View Bobbing option.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Video Settings
steps.success_cue: The Video Settings screen is open and the View Bobbing control is visible.

steps.action: Set View Bobbing to ON. If it already reads ON, leave it unchanged. Use the menu's Done buttons to return to the world.
steps.exact_input: Click "View Bobbing" only if it currently reads OFF; then select Done -> Done -> Back to Game.
steps.success_cue: The View Bobbing setting reads ON, and the player has returned to the loaded world.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory and select the Search Items tab so the required equipment can be obtained without crafting or exploration.
steps.exact_input: Press E, then select the Search Items tab marked with a compass icon.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory search field and item grid are visible.

steps.action: Search for an Elytra and place one into an empty hotbar slot. Pick up the Elytra from the search result with left-click and place it into the desired hotbar slot with another left-click.
steps.exact_input: Enter "elytra" in the search field; left-click the Elytra result; left-click an empty hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: An Elytra icon is present in the player's hotbar.

steps.action: Clear or replace the search text, search for Firework Rocket, and place Firework Rockets into a different hotbar slot.
steps.exact_input: Enter "firework rocket" in the search field; left-click a Firework Rocket result; left-click a different hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A Firework Rocket stack is present in the hotbar without replacing the Elytra.

steps.action: Open the player equipment view within the Creative inventory—the tab that displays the player model and armor slots. Drag the Elytra from the hotbar into the chest equipment slot beside the player model. The chest slot is the torso slot, second armor slot from the top.
steps.exact_input: Select the player inventory/equipment tab; left-click the Elytra in the hotbar; left-click the chest equipment slot.
steps.success_cue: The Elytra appears in the chest equipment slot and is shown equipped on the player model.

steps.action: Close the inventory and select the hotbar slot containing Firework Rockets so they can be used during Elytra flight.
steps.exact_input: Press E to close the inventory, then press the number key corresponding to the Firework Rocket hotbar slot or use the mouse wheel to select it.
steps.success_cue: A Firework Rocket is visible in the player's first-person hand, and the corresponding hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Use Creative flight to gain enough altitude for a reliable Elytra deployment. Double-tap Jump to begin Creative flight, then hold Jump to ascend until the ground is safely below the player; approximately 20 blocks or more is sufficient as an execution aid.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space, then hold Space to ascend.
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering well above the ground and no longer standing on a block.

steps.action: Prepare to transition from Creative flight into Elytra gliding. Face toward open terrain, hold Move Forward, and double-tap Jump to disable Creative flight. Allow the player to begin falling without landing.
steps.exact_input: Aim toward open terrain; hold W; double-tap Space.
steps.success_cue: The player is moving forward and beginning to lose altitude rather than hovering in Creative flight.

steps.action: While airborne and falling, press Jump once to deploy the equipped Elytra, then continue holding Move Forward and steer into a shallow forward glide.
steps.exact_input: Press Space once while falling; continue holding W and steer with the mouse.
steps.success_cue: The fall changes into controlled forward Elytra gliding, and the player remains airborne.

steps.action: Use the selected Firework Rocket while gliding to accelerate. Continue facing away from the initially generated area.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once while the Firework Rocket is selected and the Elytra is deployed.
steps.success_cue: The player receives a forward rocket boost and continues gliding through the air.

steps.action: Begin an external two-hour timer and sustain Elytra travel through newly generated terrain. Choose one general direction and continue forward rather than circling back over already loaded chunks. Hold Move Forward, steer clear of mountains and obstacles, and right-click additional Firework Rockets whenever more speed or altitude is needed. Continue for approximately two hours of active in-world flight. If terrain ahead has not rendered, reduce the descent angle or rocket frequency and wait while still in the world until chunks render; resume forward travel as soon as terrain is visible. Do not exit or reload the world during this interval.
steps.exact_input: For approximately 2 hours: hold W, steer with the mouse, and right-click with Firework Rockets as needed. Do not use Save and Quit or restart the world.
steps.success_cue: Approximately two hours of active Elytra flight have elapsed in the same world session, the player's location has advanced continuously away from the starting region, and newly rendered terrain has repeatedly appeared ahead during travel.

steps.action: After the flight interval, stop using Firework Rockets and make a controlled landing on unobstructed solid ground. Aim at a shallow angle, allow speed to decrease, and touch down without leaving the world.
steps.exact_input: Release right-click; continue steering with the mouse and W as needed until landing.
steps.success_cue: The Elytra glide has ended, the player is standing on solid ground, and ordinary grounded movement is available.

steps.action: Keep View Bobbing enabled and preserve the accumulated session state. Do not reopen the world, teleport to another world, enter another dimension, or use Save and Quit. Ensure the camera remains in first person and the hand or selected Firework Rocket remains visible before starting the walking action.
steps.exact_input: If necessary, press F5 until first-person view is restored; press F1 only if the hand and HUD are hidden.
steps.success_cue: The player is grounded in first person, the hand or held Firework Rocket is visible, and the same world session used for the two-hour flight is still active.

steps.action: Begin walking forward on the ground and maintain ordinary walking for several seconds without jumping, flying, or sprinting. This is the action at which the separate observation subsystem should inspect first-person movement and rendering.
steps.exact_input: Press and hold W for several seconds.
steps.success_cue: The player is moving forward on foot over solid ground in first person after the approximately two-hour Elytra flight.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has completed approximately two hours of continuous Elytra-and-Firework travel through newly generated chunks, landed without reloading the world, retained first-person hand visibility with View Bobbing enabled, and has just begun walking forward on solid ground. Hand control to the observation subsystem while grounded walking continues.
uncertainties: The report supplies no world seed, coordinates, biome, travel direction, required distance, or exact number of generated chunks. A new world and continuous travel in one direction are used as the simplest deterministic way to keep generating new chunks.

The report gives a variable trigger interval of about one to two hours. This plan uses approximately two hours to maximize the chance of reaching the reported condition, but the exact threshold may differ between runs or computers.

The report says to fly around while generating chunks but does not specify a route. Avoiding loops and traveling continuously away from the starting area is a practical interpretation intended to prevent travel over already generated chunks.
The exact frequency and flight duration of Firework Rocket boosts are not specified. Rockets should be used only as often as needed to maintain sustained forward Elytra travel and avoid landing.

No exact frame rate, render distance, simulation distance, hardware specification, or chunk-generation rate is supplied. These factors may change how much terrain is generated during the reported one-to-two-hour interval.
The linked video was not needed to operationalize the supplied written reproduction steps and was not consulted.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-267046:Players' heads are momentarily incorrectly positioned when entering the elytra flying state
source_meta._title: Players' heads are incorrectly positioned while exiting the swimming/crawling state when other players are on screen

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.1 in a vanilla multiplayer environment with two simultaneously connected clients. An integrated Open-to-LAN world is sufficient; a dedicated server is not required. Use Player A's display for the reproduction view. Player A must have permission to execute commands. Creative mode and a Superflat world are practical choices for safely constructing the isolated aerial glass block and positioning Player B.
preconditions: Launch both clients with Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.1, the first version listed as affected in the report.
Use two distinct connected players and designate them Player A and Player B. These labels describe their roles and do not require changing their account names.
Player A must be able to execute in-game commands with a leading slash. In an Open-to-LAN world, enable cheats when opening the world to LAN.
Use Player A's game window as the camera whose contents determine whether Player B is on screen.
Keep both clients connected and their surrounding chunks loaded throughout both the control pass and the final trigger pass.
Player A must remain stationary on the same isolated glass support block while each overhead block is added and removed.

Use the same camera perspective, look direction, graphics configuration, and general framing for the control pass and final pass; the intended changed condition is whether Player B is rendered on Player A's screen.

steps.action: On both clients, select and launch the exact Minecraft Java Edition version 1.20.1. Do not use the listed fix version 24w37a.
steps.success_cue: Both clients show Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.1 and are ready to enter the same multiplayer world.

steps.action: On Player A's client, create a new Creative-mode Superflat world. After entering it, press Esc, select Open to LAN, set the LAN game mode to Creative, enable cheats, and start the LAN world. An already prepared equivalent multiplayer world may be used instead.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Open to LAN -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Start LAN World
steps.success_cue: Player A is in a multiplayer-accessible Creative world and can execute commands.

steps.action: On Player B's client, open Multiplayer, select Player A's LAN world, and join it. Assign the hosting player the role Player A and the joining player the role Player B.
steps.exact_input: Multiplayer -> select the LAN world -> Join Server
steps.success_cue: Player A and Player B are simultaneously connected to the same world.

steps.action: Using Player A, create the isolated aerial support block. Press T to open chat, enter the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /setblock 0 100 0 minecraft:glass
steps.success_cue: A single glass block exists at X=0, Y=100, Z=0, far above the Superflat terrain.

steps.action: Using Player A, teleport to the center of the top surface of that glass block. Press T, enter the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Player A is standing at X=0.5, Y=101, Z=0.5, centered on the glass block at X=0, Y=100, Z=0.

steps.action: Confirm that the support is completely isolated in the air: Player A must be standing on the one glass block, with no horizontally or diagonally adjacent blocks and no terrain near the player. Do not place a platform around it.
steps.success_cue: The support glass is the only nearby block, Player A is stable on top of it, and the surrounding area is open air.

steps.action: On Player A's client, switch from first-person to third-person front view. With default controls, press F5 repeatedly until Player A's face and head are visible. If the perspective control was rebound, use the bound Toggle Perspective control instead.
steps.exact_input: F5
steps.success_cue: Player A can see their own head from the front in their own game window.

steps.action: Adjust Player A's camera framing without walking off the block. Keep Player A's head clearly visible and large enough for its motion to be inspected during the crawl-to-standing transition.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse only; do not use movement keys
steps.success_cue: Player A's head is clearly visible in the third-person view, and Player A remains centered on the isolated glass support.

steps.action: Move Player B near the aerial test location but outside Player A's current camera frame. In Creative mode, Player B can double-tap Space to begin flying, hold Space to ascend, use W/A/S/D to move, and use Left Shift to descend. Player B must not be rendered anywhere on Player A's screen during the control pass.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space; then use Space, Left Shift, and W/A/S/D as needed
steps.success_cue: Player B is connected and available nearby but is not visible anywhere in Player A's game view.

steps.action: Recheck Player A's display immediately before the control pass. Keep Player A stationary and verify that Player A's own head is visible while Player B is entirely out of sight and off-screen.
steps.success_cue: Player A's head is framed for inspection, Player B is absent from Player A's screen, and Player A remains centered on the support glass.

steps.action: Begin the control pass. On Player A's client, press T, enter the report's glass command exactly as written including the leading slash, and press Enter. Because the coordinates are relative, Player A—not Player B—must execute this command.
steps.exact_input: /setblock ~ ~1 ~ minecraft:glass
steps.success_cue: A glass block appears in Player A's upper-body/head space and Player A begins changing into the forced crawling/swimming pose.

steps.action: Do not move Player A. Wait until the forced crawling/swimming pose has stabilized before continuing.
steps.success_cue: Player A is visibly in the horizontal crawling/swimming pose while remaining on the isolated support block, and Player B is still absent from Player A's screen.

steps.action: Using Player A's mouse, look upward while retaining the third-person view. Keep Player A's own head visible in the frame; do not walk, jump, or change perspective.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse upward
steps.success_cue: Player A is looking upward, their head remains visible for inspection, and Player B remains off-screen.

steps.action: Trigger the report's control transition. On Player A's client, press T, enter the air command exactly as written including the leading slash, and press Enter. Keep the camera centered on Player A's head as chat closes.
steps.exact_input: /setblock ~ ~1 ~ minecraft:air
steps.success_cue: The overhead glass has been replaced with air and Player A has started leaving the crawling/swimming pose while Player B remains off-screen.

steps.action: Without evaluating or changing the camera, wait for the control transition to finish. Do not move Player A from the isolated support block.
steps.success_cue: Player A has returned to a fully upright standing pose on the same glass support and is ready for the second pass.

steps.action: Move Player B into Player A's existing camera frame. Player B may fly into position using W/A/S/D, Space, and Left Shift. Stop Player B at a location where their player model is clearly rendered on Player A's screen without blocking Player A's head.
steps.exact_input: Use W/A/S/D, Space, and Left Shift on Player B's client as needed
steps.success_cue: Player B's player model and Player A's own head are simultaneously visible on Player A's screen.

steps.action: Leave Player B stationary in that visible location. On Player A's client, confirm that the perspective is still third-person front, Player A's head is clearly framed, and Player A is still centered on the original isolated glass block.
steps.success_cue: Player B remains visibly rendered in Player A's frame, Player A's head is unobstructed, and Player A has not left the support block.

steps.action: Begin the final pass. On Player A's client, press T, enter the report's glass command exactly as written including the leading slash, and press Enter. Player A must execute the command so the relative coordinates refer to Player A.
steps.exact_input: /setblock ~ ~1 ~ minecraft:glass
steps.success_cue: A glass block appears in Player A's upper-body/head space and Player A begins changing into the forced crawling/swimming pose while Player B remains visible on-screen.

steps.action: Do not move either player. Wait until Player A's crawling/swimming pose has stabilized, and make sure Player B remains rendered in Player A's view.
steps.success_cue: Player A is stably in the crawling/swimming pose on the isolated support, and Player B is still visibly rendered on Player A's screen.

steps.action: Using Player A's mouse, look upward again. Keep the same third-person perspective and keep Player A's head visible. If the changed look angle moves Player B out of frame, reposition only Player B until Player B is visible again; do not move Player A.
steps.exact_input: Move Player A's mouse upward; reposition Player B with W/A/S/D, Space, or Left Shift only if needed
steps.success_cue: Player A is looking upward in the crawling/swimming pose, Player A's head is clearly visible, and Player B is simultaneously visible in the same frame.

steps.action: Stabilize the final test framing. Stop all movement on both clients, keep Player B visible, and keep the view centered closely on Player A's head. Do not change perspective after this point.
steps.success_cue: Both player models are stationary and visible on Player A's screen, with Player A's head framed for the imminent transition.

steps.action: On Player A's client, press T and prepare the report's air command exactly as written. Do not submit a different command, and do not let Player B leave the frame.
steps.exact_input: /setblock ~ ~1 ~ minecraft:air
steps.success_cue: The exact air command is entered in Player A's chat input, Player B remains on-screen, and the command is ready to be submitted.

steps.action: Press Enter once on Player A's client to execute the prepared air command. Immediately hand control to the observation subsystem without moving either player, changing perspective, or waiting for the short exit animation to finish.
steps.exact_input: Enter
steps.success_cue: The overhead glass has just been replaced with air and Player A has begun exiting the crawling/swimming state while Player B is still visibly rendered on Player A's screen.

stor.handoff_condition: Player A has just submitted `/setblock ~ ~1 ~ minecraft:air`; the overhead block is now air, Player A's crawl-to-standing transition has begun, Player A's own head is closely framed in third-person front view, and Player B remains visibly rendered on Player A's screen. Begin observation immediately before the transient exit animation completes.
uncertainties: The report requires two players but does not specify whether to use an integrated LAN world or a dedicated server. The plan uses an Open-to-LAN world as the simplest multiplayer implementation.
The report does not specify a game mode or world type. Creative mode and a Superflat world are practical choices that permit safe aerial positioning and do not replace any stated condition.
The report does not specify exact coordinates for the isolated glass support. X=0, Y=100, Z=0 is a deterministic practical choice for a Superflat world.

The report says Player A should watch their own head but does not name a camera perspective. Third-person front view is selected because it exposes Player A's head clearly while allowing Player B to be rendered in the same view.

The report does not specify an exact upward pitch, field of view, distance, or Player B position. Player B must be adjusted so they remain visibly rendered after Player A looks upward, while Player A's head also remains unobstructed.
The contents of the attached MC-265399.mp4 were not supplied, so this plan relies on the written reproduction instructions and does not infer additional camera placement from the video.
